uncited: **Inputs:** A list of strokes, where each stroke has an associated color, opacity map, and height map.
The background is initialized to black with full opacity.
**Outputs:** A final RGB image with simulated paint depth and lighting.
**Color Buffer:** Stores the RGB components of the base stroke colors.
**Overlap Weight Buffer:** Stores the red component of the color buffer after the Overlap Pass.
Represents the count of overlapping strokes.
**Height Buffer:** Stores the red component of the color buffer after the Height Pass.
Represents the height map value of the last drawn stroke.
**Color Pass:** Draw each stroke colored and textured with an opacity map.
Save the RGB components in the Color Buffer.
*   Stroke color is set to $(1,1,1,\alpha)$.
*   This pass records the base color information.
**Overlap Pass:** Draw each stroke white and textured with the same opacity maps used in the Color Pass.
Alpha blend with transparency $0 < \alpha \le 1$ to count overlapping strokes.
Save the red component of the color buffer in the Overlap Weight Buffer.
**Height Pass:** Draw each stroke white and textured with the height map paired with the opacity map.
Each pixel $p_i$ contains the grey value (height value) of the last stroke drawn at $p_i$.
Save the red component of the color buffer in the Height Buffer.
*   This pass records the local texture height of the most recent stroke.

**Height Field Calculation:** For each pixel $p_i$, compute the final height value $h(p_i)$ as the sum of the stroke’s height map value at $p_i$ plus a weight representing the number of strokes overlapping at $p_i$.

**Final Rendering:** For each pixel $p_i$, combine the stroke’s diffuse color components (from Color Pass) and the surface normal (from Height Pass) using the Phong model to obtain the final RGB color value.
*   **Stroke Orientation Approximation:** Bézier curves approximate, not interpolate, control points.
The curve may not pass through control points B and C but is pulled in their direction.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of strokes and image resolution, as it requires three passes over the stroke list and one pass over the image for shading.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for three buffers (Color, Overlap, Height) of size proportional to the image resolution.
*   **Limitations:** Relies on the assumption that stroke overlap can be approximated by alpha blending, which may not perfectly represent physical paint accumulation in all cases.
